answer: A timber exchange on a ridge treats glowing feedback as a fable unless it comes from a settled trade with an irrevocably burned fee. Reputation rises by at most one unit per credit burned, not by review count or new accounts; the ledger counts each fee receipt once. A buyer and seller may be aliases of one farm, but self-trading still destroys credits. Manufacturing R reputation therefore costs at least R credits however many keys are used. This needs a fee asset that is costly to acquire and no signup rebates; it prices reputation fraud but cannot stop rich attackers buying influence.
